newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria police signals crackdown on crime.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria police signals crackdown on crime.

text.p: Bulgaria's police director said on Thursday his men had "uncovered" 17,000 more crimes in the first six months this year than in the same period last year.
But a true comparison could not be made with last year's figures because they had been falsified by the country's former Socialist rulers, he said.
Slavcho Bosilkov, director of the National Police, told a news conference that official crime figures had been artificially reduced in 1995 and 1996 under the previous government.
He said crimes reported were not registered. Written reports were kept
in drawers and no action was taken.
Thefts of agricultural produce and farm property as well as about 40
per cent of minor crimes had not been registered by police in 1995 and 1996.
"This has been aimed at lowering artificially the level of crime,"
Bosilkov said.
The public refrained from reporting police racketeering and blackmail
attempts because they feared they would not be protected.
The ex-communist Socialist government was toppled in February after 30
days of street protests.
Bosilkov said the public now felt more protected by the law and their trust in the police had grown.
"In the first six months of the year police have uncovered some
17,000 crimes more than the same period last year," he said.
Bulgaria's new government, which took office in May, has vowed to stem
the crime and corruption which flourished in the seven years since the end of one-party rule.
Last month parliament adopted amendments to the outdated penal and criminal laws to speed up the fight against crime .
Prime Minister Ivan Kostov voiced concern recently that organised crime threatened to destroy state authority in Bulgaria and had virtually replaced it in some parts of the country.
